title: Emrys and the Crown
premise: Felix Fairweather, last apprentice of the Fairweather charm-sellers, has survived ten years in Greyhollow by selling trinkets that do nothing—until a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands and dies whispering about a king unmade. The map leads to the Emberline, a hidden network of outlawed mages who believe King Aldric has been hollowed out and replaced by a crown-born parasite called the Regent. Pursued by the Crown's witch-hunters and betrayed by the one ally he trusts most, Felix discovers his 'useless' charms are the last living thread of a binding spell his guild was founded to maintain—and that only a Fairweather can rebind or release the king. In the end, Felix chooses neither to destroy the Regent nor restore the old order, but to bind the crown itself so no one can wear it, finding at last a family among the outlaws who fought beside him.
about_author: Petra Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a drafty cottage on the Welsh borders, where she shares a garden with an opinionated population of toads.

chapters.title: The Charm That Did Nothing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On the eve of the guild's final bankruptcy, Felix sells a luck-charm to a frightened child, lying as he always does: it's just brass and wishful thinking. A raid by witch-hunters scatters the market, and Felix hides his grandfather's ledger—the guild's true inheritance. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a stubborn ember of hope.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A bleeding woman collapses in his shop at closing time, pressing a wax-sealed map into his hands and gasping that 'the king is not the king' before dying. Witch-hunters arrive minutes behind her; Felix barely escapes through the cellar with the map and her signet ring. Emotional beat: terror and the vertigo of a life upended.

chapters.title: Greyhollow After Dark
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, fleeing through the city's rooftops and sewers with hunter Captain Vess tracking him. He deciphers the map's first marker: a chalk sigil beneath the old tannery bridge. There he meets Sable, a sharp-tongued smuggler who recognizes the seal and, instead of robbing him, offers passage. Emotional beat: first fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Emberline
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She leads Felix downriver to a flooded quarry where the Emberline—an underground fellowship of outlawed hedge-mages—keeps its hearth. Its leader, Mother Quill, recognizes the dead woman's ring and mourns her: she was Quill's daughter. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes belonging offered.

chapters.title: What the Guild Was For
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Quill reveals the truth: the Fairweather guild were binders, maintaining spells that kept dangerous things caged—including, long ago, something buried beneath the capital. His 'useless' charms are dormant anchors. Felix rages at ten years of lies, then agrees to learn. Emotional beat: anger curdling into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: Lessons in Small Magic
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Training montage among the Emberline: Felix learns to wake his charms, clumsy but startlingly strong—his bloodline runs thick with binding craft. He befriends Wren, a feral young fire-speaker, and old Tam, who lost his voice to a hunter's brand. Emotional beat: joy rediscovered, family forming.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Emberline's spy returns from the capital with proof: King Aldric's eyes have gone flat glass-grey; decrees now come signed in a hand no courtier recognizes. The thing called the Regent wears him like a glove. Quill declares the mission: reach the king before the coronation of the Regent's heir. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Captain Vess
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The witch-hunter captain interrogates Felix's neighbors and finds the ledger page he dropped—a Fairweather name. Vess, herself once saved by an illegal charm, begins quietly doubting the hunt she serves. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: Road Through Ashfen
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The company travels disguised as pilgrims; in plague-struck Ashfen, Felix breaks cover to use a warming charm for dying children, exposing them all. Vess's hunters descend. Sable covers their escape and takes a crossbow bolt meant for Felix. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of a good heart.

chapters.title: The Field Surgeon's Table
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, fevered and drifting. Felix works through the night with binding magic, stitching Sable's wound closed with woven charms—the first great working of his life. When she wakes, she tells him why she never stays anywhere: everyone leaves or dies. He answers: not this time. Emotional beat: love admitted sideways.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Mark
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (told through Wren reading his slate). Someone in the Emberline is feeding the Crown their route. Suspicion poisons the camp; Wren accuses Quill's surviving son, Corvin, who denies it too smoothly. Felix defends him—and will regret it. Emotional beat: paranoia gnawing at found family.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weir
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Hunters trap the company at a river weir; the ambush is precise—they knew the plan. Tam dies holding the crossing so the others flee upstream. In the chaos, Felix glimpses Corvin signaling the hunters. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal fused into cold fury.

chapters.title: Judgment Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. The Emberline holds its own trial for Corvin in the marshes—no gallows, no crown courts. Corvin confesses: Vess holds his daughter hostage. Quill must choose exile or execution; she chooses exile, and the fellowship fractures over her mercy. Emotional beat: justice weighed against vengeance.

chapters.title: The Capital's Gilded Rot
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Infiltrating the capital during festival week, they see the Regent's rule up close: charm-burnings in the square, a king paraded like a puppet who sometimes weeps without knowing why. Felix sees Aldric's face and recognizes the same hollowness his grandfather's ledger described. Emotional beat: horror made intimate.

chapters.title: Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Using the signet ring, Wren and Felix breach the palace undercrofts and find the original binding site—a sealed door older than the kingdom, scratched from the inside. The Regent isn't wearing the king; it's leaking out of what the first binders buried. Emotional beat: awe tipping into fear.

chapters.title: Vess Turns Her Coat
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to burn a village of charm-keepers, Vess refuses, frees her prisoners, and delivers the palace guard rotations to the Emberline instead—paying her debt to the unknown charmer who once saved her. Emotional beat: redemption chosen at ruinous price.

chapters.title: The Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Everything converges: the Regent plans to bind itself permanently into the royal bloodline tomorrow. Quill's plan requires a Fairweather to stand at the binding door while the king is pulled free—but whoever holds the door may not walk away. Felix volunteers before anyone can argue. Emotional beat: quiet acceptance of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Storming the Glass Court
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The Emberline strikes during the coronation vigil: Wren fires the granary as diversion, Sable cuts the puppeteer-strings of the court, Vess holds the gates against her former brothers-in-arms. Felix fights his way to the throne room where the Regent speaks with Aldric's stolen mouth. Emotional beat: desperate, blazing momentum.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the undercroft door, Felix unravels the ancient binding and pulls the Regent out of Aldric—but the thing offers him everything he ever wanted: a full guild, a father's pride, a city where magic is legal. He refuses, and binds the Regent into the crown itself, sealing it forever. Emotional beat: temptation overcome by love of flawed, real people.

chapters.title: What a Crown Is Worth
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. The bound crown cannot safely be worn by anyone; Aldric, half-hollowed, abdicates and names a council drawn from guilds and commons alike. Some call it treason; the streets call it dawn. Vess is pardoned by the new council's first act. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect hope.

chapters.title: The Fairweather Sign
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Back in Greyhollow, Felix reopens the shop—not selling useless charms, but teaching small honest magic to anyone who knocks. Sable stays, arguing about signage; Wren burns the first batch of stock. The guild sign goes back up, repainted by many hands. Emotional beat: homecoming, warmth after long cold.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Crown
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, years later. A student asks why the shop bears two names—Fairweather above the door, Emrys carved beneath, the old binder-word for 'the one who holds the door.' Felix tells the story whole for the first time, ending where it began: some things are kept not by kings, but by the people who choose each other. Emotional beat: peace, legacy, belonging earned.
